questions.text: Which of the following statements can be inferred from the passage ?

options.text: Entrepreneurship is not at all worth the risk.
Entrepreneurs have a higher chance of earning as much or more than salaried workers when they go back to the workplace.
The labor market does not encourage those entrepreneurs who have failed in their ideas.
People should first do a salaried job and then move on to entrepreneurship.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2)

  • Entrepreneurship may fail but it doesn't mean we should not try it. 
  • According to the passage, entrepreneurship can bring us a good amount of money.
  • As per the passage, the labor market gives equal chances to those entrepreneurs who have failed in their ideas.
  • It is not stated anywhere that we should first try to do a job then go for entrepreneurship.
  • Thus, we can say that option 2, only can be inferred from the passage.

questions.text: According to the author, how can entrepreneurship pay off in financial terms ?

options.text: When the entrepreneurs are just driven only by the ideas of being their own boss and by their personal passion.
When the entrepreneurs persevere and stay longer than two years working on their ideas.
When the skills developed during self-employment give more monetary advantage on returning to the workforce.
Entrepreneurs who fail in their ideas are not able to earn more than the salaried workers with similar characteristics.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 5)

  • "At the same time, entrepreneurs who stay longer than two years, make substantially more than similar salaried workers.”
  • Maybe the skills developed during [a] self-employment spell are useful as [a] salaried worker.”
  • These two sentences are directly given in the passage and we can deduce the correct options from these lines.

questions.text: Which of the following are not concluded by Manso's findings ?

It can be explained clearly that entrepreneurs earn less in their next job.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 4)

  • The information given in options 1, 2 & 3 can be inferred from the passage.
  • There is nothing found in the passage as per statement 4 because 'next job pays as much or more than the entrepreneur would have made if they’d never been self-employed.'
  • The passage says : "he found that individuals who had been self-employed at one point in their career fared better.." but option 2 says fare worse.
  • Hence, the answer will be option 5.

questions.text:
Below a word is given followed by three sentences which consist of that word. Identify the sentence/s which best expresses the meaning of the word. Choose option 5 (None of these) if the word is not suitable in any of the sentences.

A. The smooth polyamide provides an athletic-looking fit and there's a cool buckle detail at the waist to complete this great trunk.

B. Her hands were shaking and her knees wanted to buckle.

C. The general average yields of the corn crops are not comparable one with the other, because they are given by measure and not by weight, whereas the weight per buckle varies considerably.
questions.explanation:

2. fasten or decorate with a buckle especially one's seat belt in a car or aircraft.

3. bend and give way under pressure or strain.

Among these, the meaning given in 1, makes statement A correct. the meaning in 3 makes statement B correct.

questions.text:
In the question below, three statements are given which may or may not be grammatically correct. Identify the statement/statements that is/are incorrect.

I.No sooner did I speak, than he left.

II. The patient was accompanied with his friend.

III.Mr. Sharma may be late but I am sure Mr. Kapoor won't be.
questions.explanation:
Statements I and III are contextually and grammatically correct.

Key Points

In statement II, by will replace with because –
by (Prep.) is used for indicating the agent/object after a Passive Verb in case of Passive Voice.
Agent/Object = his friend & Passive Verb = accompanied
With (Prep.) indicates being in the company of
e.g - His friend stayed with him in the hospital.
        He was knocked down by a bus.

Additional Information

In statement II: the usage of 'No sooner....than' is correct whenever we use 'no sooner' an adverb at the starting of the sentence, use the inversion form of the verb.  

Correct Statement II: The patient was accompanied (Passive verb) with/by his friend (Object). [as the given sentence is in the Passive Voice.]
Thus, the correct answer is option 2.

questions.text:
In the question below, three statements are given which may or may not be grammatically correct. Identify the statement/statements that is/are incorrect.

I. Young people in Britain eats more snacks than people of the same age in other European countries.

II. He spends a good deal of money on eating out.

III. Without waiting for the instructions from the Government, some cable operators in the city had block the news.
questions.explanation:
• Statement II is contextually and grammatically correct.
     
  • In statement I, the usage of the word eats is incorrect.

The subject - young people - is Plural and thus must agree with a Plural verb. Thus, 'eat' will replace eats to rectify the incorrect sentence.

Correct Statement I: Young people in Britain eats / eat more snacks than people of the same age in other European countries.

  • In statement III, the usage of the word block is incorrect.

Correct structutre of sentence with 'had'-Past Perfect Tense: Subject + had + v3 + object + other words.

According to the structure, Had is followed by V3.
But in statement III, Had is followed by 'block' - V1, that should be replaced with blocked'-V3 for making the sentence grammatically correct.

Correct statement III. Without waiting for the instructions from the Government, some cable operators in the city had block / blocked the news.

Thus, Option 5 is the correct answer.

questions.text:
In the question below, three statements are given which may or may not be grammatically correct. Identify the statement/statements that is/are incorrect.

I. When shall we arrive to our destination?

II. Neither Rohit nor Mohit were there at the restaurant when I went there.

III. Ten kilometres is a long distance to walk.
questions.explanation:
Statement III is contextually and grammatically correct.

In statement I, the usage of word to is incorrect.
at will replace to because –
We usually say that someone arrives at a place vs arrives in a country/city.
e.g: We arrived at the station at 3 o'clock.
       The President arrived in Rome today.

Correct sentence I: When shall we arrive to / at our destination?

In statement II, the usage of the word were is incorrect.
When there are 2 different subjects that are joined by either____or/ neither____nor / not only____but also/ __or__ ,and are different in numbers, the subject closer to the verb decides whether the verb will be singular or plural,

  • For e.g: There is / are either some boys (subject closer to the verb ) or a girl in the class.
  • Neither the ministers nor the King (subject closer to the verb) have / has been arrested.
  • Not only Sapna but also her friends (subject closer to the verb) has / have come. 
     

Here, the subject closer to the verb 'were' is Mohit and thus the verb ‘were’ will be replaced by was to agree with the Singular subject.
Correct sentence II. Neither Rohit nor Mohit were / was there at the restaurant when I went there. 

Thus, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.text:
In each question, one sentence is given in which certain words are in bold and numbered from A to E. Below the sentence are given five options with  possible pairs of interchange of those bold words. Choose the pair(s) of words which are needed to be interchanged to make the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful.

Radical feminists seek to (A)liberate patriarchy by (B)challenging existing social (C)norms and institutions, and believe that (D)eliminating patriarchy will (E)abolish everyone from an unjust society.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. A-E.

questions.text: Milk and water are mixed in vessel A in the ratio of 3 : 7 and in the vessel B in the ratio of 5 : 7. In what ratio should quantities be taken from the two vessels so as to form a mixture in which milk and water will be in the ratio 17 : 28?

GIVEN :

Milk and water are mixed in vessel A in the ratio of 3 : 7.

∴ quantity of milk = 3/10

Milk and water are mixed in vessel B in the ratio of 5 : 7

∴ quantity of milk = 5/12

These two are mixed together to get milk and water in ratio 17 : 28

Quantity of milk in mixture = 17/45

 

CONCEPT :

Replacement of Mixtures.

 

ASSUMPTION :

Let the ratio from vessel A be ‘a’.

∴ Ratio from vessel B = 1 – a

 

CALCULATION :

\(\begin{array}{l} \therefore \frac{3}{{10}}a + \frac{5}{{12}}\left( {1 - a} \right) = \frac{{17}}{{45}}\\ \Rightarrow \frac{{3a}}{{10}} + \frac{5}{{12}} - \frac{{5a}}{{12}} = \frac{{17}}{{45}}\\ \Rightarrow \frac{5}{{12}} - \frac{{17}}{{45}} = \frac{{7a}}{{60}}\\ \Rightarrow \frac{7}{{180}} = \frac{{7a}}{{60}} \end{array}\)

⇒ a = 1/3

Ratio for vessel B = 1 – a = 2/3

∴ Ratio of quantities from vessel A and vessel B \(= \frac{1}{3}:\frac{2}{3}\)

= 1 : 2

questions.text: A person travels from X to Y at a constant speed. If his speed was increased by 10 km/hour, it would have taken one hour lesser to cover the distance. It would have taken further 45 minutes lesser if the speed was further increased by 10 km/h. Find the distance between X and Y.

Let ‘s’ be the speed of the person and ‘t’ be the time taken by the person to cover the distance between X and Y.

If his speed were increase by 10 km/h, it would have been taken one hour lesser or cover the distance.

⇒ st = (s+10) (t – 1)

⇒ st = st – s + 10t – 10

⇒ 10t – s = 10      ---- (1)

It would have taken further 45 minutes lesser if the speed was further increased by 10 km/h.

⇒ \(st = \left( {s + 20} \right)\left( {t - 1\frac{3}{4}} \right)\)

\(\Rightarrow st = st - \frac{7}{4}\;s + 20t - 35\)

\(\Rightarrow 20t - \frac{7}{4}\;s = 35\)

⇒ 80t - 7s = 140      ---- (2)

Multiply (1) by 7

70t – 7s = 70      ---- (3)

From (2) and (3)

10t = 70

⇒ t = 7 hours

Put this value of t in (1)

10 × 7 – s = 10

⇒ s = 60 km/hr

Distance = st = 60 × 7 = 420 km

A woman’s efficiency = y/day

A child's efficiency = z/day

⇒ 5x + 6y + 4z = 1/10      ----(1)

⇒ 6y + 6z = 1/20      ----(2)

⇒ 2x + 6y = 1/18      ----(3)

From (1) - (2) we get,

\(\Rightarrow 5x - 2z = \frac{1}{{10}} - \frac{1}{{20}}\)

\(\Rightarrow 5x - 2z = \frac{1}{{20}}\)      ----(4)

From (1) - (3) we get,

\(\Rightarrow 3x + 4z = \frac{1}{{10}} - \frac{1}{{18}}\)

\(\Rightarrow 3x + 4z = \frac{2}{{45}}\)      ----(5)

From (4) and (3) we get,

⇒ x = 1/90

Putting the value of x in (3),

\(\Rightarrow \frac{2}{{90}} + 6y = \frac{1}{{18}}\)

⇒ y = 1/180

Let, 2 men and 1 woman can complete the work in = a days

According to problem,

\(\Rightarrow \frac{2}{{90}} + \frac{1}{{180}} = \frac{1}{a}\)

\(\Rightarrow \frac{1}{a} = \frac{5}{{180}}\)

⇒ a = 36

∴ 2 men and 1 woman can complete the work in 36 days.

questions.text: A person can row a boat from A to B upstream in 4 hours 30 minutes, and downstream in 3 hours. If the speed of the stream is 2 km/hr, find the speed of the boat in still water.

Speed with the stream is the speed of the boat downstream, and speed against the stream is the Speed of the boat upstream.

Let the Speed of the boat downstream be ‘a’ km/hr and Speed of the boat upstream be ‘b’ km/hr.

Let the distance travelled upstream be ‘d’ km.

We know that,

Time = Distance/Speed

Time upstream = d / b = 4.5   (∵ 1 hr = 60 min)

⇒ d = 4.5b

Time downstream = d / a = 3

⇒ d = 3a

Equating,

3a = 4.5b

⇒ a = 1.5b

We know that,

Speed of the stream = ½ (Speed of the boat downstream- Speed of the boat upstream)

⇒ 2 = ½ (a - b)

⇒ 4 = a - b

⇒ 4 = 1.5b - b

⇒ 0.5 b = 4

⇒ b = 8 km/hr

⇒ a = 1.5(8) = 12 km/hr

We know that,

Speed of boat in still water = ½ (Speed of the boat downstream+ Speed of the boat upstream)

⇒ Speed of boat in still water = ½ (12 + 8) = ½ (20) = 10 km/hr

∴ Speed of boat in still water = 10 km/hr

questions.text: Two trains having lengths of 90 m and 110 m are running on parallel track in the same direction with slower trains running at a speed of 45 km/h. The train, having a length of 110 m, crosses a man in the slower train in 18 s. Find the speed of the faster train.
questions.explanation:
Given speed of slower train V1 = 45 km/h

Let the speed of faster train V2 = V km/h

Since both the trains are moving in parallel direction.

∴ Relative speed = V2 – V1 = V – 45

∴ To cross a man in the smaller train longer train has to cross it’s own length with relative speed

Time taken to cross the 110 m length = 18 s

Speed = Distance/Time

⇒ (V – 45) × (1000/3600) = 110/18               (since 1 km/h = (1000/3600) m/s)

 ⇒ V – 45 = (110/18) × (3600/1000)             [(3600/1000) m/s = 1 km/h]

⇒ V – 45 = 22

⇒ V = 67 km/h

∴ Speed of longer train = 67 km/h

questions.text: A person invested a sum of Rs. 4000 at compound interest for 3 years at 10% per annum rate of interest. How much money should he invest at simple interest so that he earns the same amount of interest at 10% rate of interest in 4 years?

Given:

At compound interest:

Principal = Rs. 4000

Time period = 3 years

Rate of interest = 10% per annum

Formula used:

Simple Interest = (Principal × Rate × Time)/100

Compound Interest = Principal[(1 + Rate/100)n – 1]

Calculation:

C.I. = P(1 + r/100)n - P

⇒ C.I. = 4000(1 + 10/100)3 - 4000

⇒ C.I. = 4000 × (1.1)3 - 4000

⇒ C.I. = 5324 - 4000

⇒ C.I. = Rs.1324

Now, 

S.I. = PRT/100

⇒ 1324 = (P × 10 × 4)/100

⇒ P = (1324 × 100)/(10 × 4) 

⇒ P = Rs.3310

∴ The required answer is Rs. 3310.

questions.text: The speed of a car is 1.5 times the speed of a bus. If the speed of the car is 60 km/hr then what will be the difference in the time taken by the bus and the time taken by the car to cover a distance of 720 km?

Let the speed of bus be x km/hr.

Then, the speed of car = 1.5x = 60 km/hr

Therefore, speed of bus = 40 km/hr

Now, time taken by car to cover 720 km = 720/ 60 = 12 hr

 Time taken by bus to cover 720 km = 720/ 40 = 18 hr

Thus, difference in the time taken by the bus and the time taken by the car to cover 720 km = (18 – 12) hr = 6 hr.

questions.text: If 9 men, 6 women and 6 children can do a piece of work in 8 days, 16 women and 6 children can do the same work in 10 days and 6 men and 10 women can do the same work in 10 days then in how many days will 2 men and 10 women will complete the same work?

9M + 6W + 6C = 8      ------(1)

16W + 6C = 10      ------(2)

6M + 10W = 10      ------(3)

⇒ 6M = 6W + 6C

⇒ M = W + C      ------(4)

By equation 1 and equation 3

[9M + 6(W + C)] × 8 = (6M + 10W) × 10

⇒ (9M + 6M) × 8 = (6M + 10W) × 10

⇒ 120M = 60M + 100W

⇒ 60M = 100W

⇒ 3M = 5W      ------(4)

Using equation 3 and equation 4

2 men and 10 women will complete the same work in:

 [(6M + 10W) × 10]/(2M + 10W)

⇒ [(6M + 6M) × 10]/(2M + 6M)

⇒ 120M/8M

⇒ 15 days
